Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quarterly review: capacity playbook + unit economics (QBR prep)

Team —

As we start QBR prep for next week, I want one concise deliverable for leadership that ties:
- projected GPU spend for next quarter (by pool / reserved vs burst)
- utilization targets and headroom assumptions
- batching & KV/prefix caching levers and estimated token-cost impact
- risk scenarios (major model rollouts, region failover)

Can each of you take the following slices and update the attached workbook (capacity_projection_v3.xlsx):
- Marcus: run the reserved vs burst forecast, include a 90/95th percentile demand curve and three sizing options (conservative, baseline, aggressive).
- Evelyn: provide utilization targets by model family and the operational runbook for autoscale thresholds.
- Laura: quantify batching/caching assumptions — expected effective token reduction from continuous batching and prefix cache hit rate at 95th pct.
- Vivek: summarize cost math and a one-page unit-economics slide that maps raw GPU $/hr to $/1k tokens delivered under each configuration.

Key ask: I need a one-page executive summary + the workbook by EOD Tue (2027-02-09) so I can fold into the QBR deck. Include assumptions inline (latency SLOs, p99 tail targets, warm KV cache hit assumptions).

Attachments: capacity_projection_v3.xlsx (WORKBOOK, sheets: demand_curve, sizing_options, cache_modeling)

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quarterly review: capacity playbook + unit economics (QBR prep)

Stephanie — thanks, jumping on this. Quick notes from the demand-side model I dropped into the workbook:

Summary (high level)
- Baseline: commit to 120 A100-equivalent GPU months / week of steady-state reserved capacity; burst to 180 for 6 hours/day at peak.
- Conservative: reserve 90, burst to 150. Aggressive: reserve 150, burst to 220.

Observations
- Peak profile skew increases with new latency-sensitive customers; 95th percentile uplift from baseline looks ~1.35x if we onboard Acadia's full NLP pipeline.
- If we keep current batching strategy unchanged, effective tokens served per GPU-hour improves ~1.8x during throughput windows but drops back for low qps tails.

Questions for ops: what are our preferred auto-scale cooldowns? If cool-down is > 3m, burst benefits diminish because of startup time for large capacity blocs.

Attachment: capacity_projection_v3.xlsx (updated demand_curve and sizing_options)

- Marcus
Senior Capacity Planner
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quarterly review: capacity playbook + unit economics (QBR prep)

Quick note — adding the autoscale thresholds and utilization targets into the workbook (sheet: sizing_options -> ops_runbook). TL;DR:

- Target steady utilization: 60% avg GPU util across reserved pools to preserve headroom for cold-starts/migrations.
- Scale-up: trigger when p95 latency > 0.9x SLO for 3 consecutive minutes or when queue length > 2000 tokens.
- Scale-down: cooldown of 5 minutes to avoid oscillation; use predictive headroom for scheduled peak windows.

Regarding caching: I validated that our prefix/KV cache gives diminishing returns below 20 tokens prefix reuse per request; we'll add a sensitivity table.

Evelyn
Director, Reliability Engineering
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quarterly review: capacity playbook + unit economics (QBR prep)

Folks — I updated caching and batching modeling with two scenarios and conservative hit-rate assumptions. Key pieces to call out for the one-pager:

Batching scenarios (sheet: cache_modeling)
- Continuous batching aggressive: average batch size 28 tokens/request leading to effective 2.3x tokens/GPU-hour for steady throughput windows (assumes low sampling overhead and optimized kernel path).
- Conservative batching: average batch size 14 -> ~1.4x tokens/GPU-hour.

KV/Prefix cache modeling
- Baseline hit-rate: 22% (current observed across traffic mix). With small changes to request routing and TTLs we can push to 30% for curated customers (Acadia will likely require higher cache TTLs).
- Net effect: moving from 22% -> 30% reduces token consumption by ~8-10% in the cost model; combined with aggressive batching this compounds to ~30% lower GPU-hours.

Risks to call out in slide:
- Large model upgrades (bigger context windows) can erode batching effectiveness and raise memory-footprint per GPU, increasing slot churn.
- Region failover: cross-region cold cache rebuild increases short-term token cost by 40-60% for impacted routes.

Attachment: unit_econ_runbook.pdf (one-page unit econ math + assumptions)

Laura
Head of Product, Redwood Console

Team — final pass attached. I merged the numbers into a one-page executive summary and added the unit economics slide you asked for. Highlights:

Executive summary (one-liner)
- Recommended baseline: reserve 120 units, keep burst to 180; hedge via a short-term marketplace burst contract for major onboarding windows. Expected delta vs current spend: +12% gross GPU $/mo but ~18-25% lower effective $/1k tokens when aggressive batching + improved cache hit-rate are enabled.

Unit economics (math)
- Raw GPU $/hr (A100 equiv): $3.75
- Conservative tokens/GPU-hour: 350k -> $0.0107 / 1k tokens
- Aggressive batching + 30% cache: 600k tokens/GPU-hour -> $0.00625 / 1k tokens

Scenario table (in workbook)
- Conservative: keep reserve = 90; expected $/1k tokens = $0.0135
- Baseline (recommend): reserve = 120; expected $/1k tokens = $0.0098
- Aggressive: reserve = 150; expected $/1k tokens = $0.0069

Open items before I hand to you for QBR deck (Stephanie):
- Confirm if finance is ok with the ~12% spend uptick to enable the latency and availability headroom. (LR: submit to finance for approval).
- Approve the marketplace burst contract for March onboarding (I attached the draft SOW in Drive link).

Attachments: unit_econ_runbook.pdf, capacity_projection_v3.xlsx

--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Finance & Ops
Redwood Inference
